p:cNvPr.descr: This diagram shows the desensitization of the beta-adrenergic receptor in the continued presence of epinephrine. This diagram shows the desensitization of the beta-adrenergic receptor in the continued presence of epinephrine across five stages. The drawing, which is a long, shaped like a backward S lined with small light blue balls on either end, representing the plasma membrane. In the first stage, the binding of epinephrine (E) to beta-adrenergic receptor triggers the dissociation of Gs beta gamma from Gs alpha (not shown). Epinephrine is represented with a small brown structure, whereas the beta-adrenergic receptor is represented by a pinkish-tan structure with folded ribbons in it. The Gs beta gamma is represented by a green oval sitting on a green double-headed projection that is connected to one of the plasma membranes. A black arrow outside the membrane points to another receptor site, connected to the Gs beta gamma structure and a blue, rounded rectangle labeled beta ARK and two circles labeled P. Here, Gsbg recruits beta ARK to the membrane, where it phosphorylates Ser residues at the carboxyl terminus of the receptor. Another long arrow on the outside of the membrane points to the third stage, where b-Arrestin (Beta-arr) binds to the phosphorylated carboxyl-terminal domain of the receptor. Beta-arr is represented by an orange rectangle with rounded edges connected to the two Ps from stage 2; the two Ps are now bound to the plasma membrane. Another arrow on the outside of the membrane points to stage 4 of the process, where the receptor-arrestin complex enters the cell by endocytosis. The brown rectangle with rounded edges is still connected to the two Ps, which are still connected to the plasma membrane next to the receptor site. The epinephrine is no longer attached to the receptor site. An arrow points to the fifth stage from the receptor site in stage 4, represented by a circular version of the backward S-like structure described in stage 1. Here, there are two receptor sites on opposite sides of the circle. The receptor site on the left-hand side is bound to the two Ps at the plasma membrane, which are bound to the brown rectangular structure. There is an arrow pointing from this receptor to another brown rectangular structure, which is pointed to the beta-arr in stage 3. In stage 5, the arrestin dissociates from the endocytic vesicle, and the receptor is dephosphorylated and returned to cell surface.
